Fit every ordered pair of a smoothed-association matrix

Source: R/fit.R
janusplot_fit.Rd

Fits gam(x_j ~ s(x_i) + <adjust>) once for every ordered pair of numeric variables and returns a janusplot_fit object holding the per-pair results, a per-cell summary table, a cleaned copy of the data used and the fit settings. janusplot() draws the matrix; summary() returns the per-cell table.

Usage

janusplot_fit(
  data,
  vars = NULL,
  adjust = NULL,
  k = -1L,
  bs = "tp",
  engine = c("bam", "gam"),
  method = NULL,
  na_action = c("pairwise", "complete"),
  n_grid = NULL,
  derivatives = 1:2,
  derivative_ci = c("pointwise", "none", "simultaneous"),
  derivative_ci_nsim = 1000L,
  p_adjust = c("none", "BH", "holm"),
  shape_cutoffs = janusplot_shape_cutoffs(),
  k_check_thresholds = NULL,
  auto_refit_k = FALSE,
  k_max_iter = 2L,
  discrete = FALSE,
  nthreads = 1L,
  parallel = FALSE,
  keep_fits = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'janusplot_fit'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'janusplot_fit'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame. Column names need not be syntactic; fits run under internal aliases and every result reports the original names.

vars

Character vector of numeric column names to fit, in matrix order. NULL (the default) takes every numeric column of data. Identical or exactly collinear columns are not fitted against each other; their cells are listed in flags$failed.

adjust

One-sided formula of covariates and random effects added to every pairwise model, for example ~ s(age) + s(site, bs = "re"). NULL (the default) fits unadjusted smooths. Character and logical adjust columns are converted to factor before fitting. Random-effect smooths are excluded from prediction, so the curve and its band are population-level. With the identity link (the Gaussian default) the curve is the smooth averaged over the adjustment covariates of the data, and the plots draw each point as a partial residual: the observation with its own adjustment replaced by that average, so points and curve share one level (style$adjusted_points). With another link, numeric covariates are held at their mean and fixed factors at their most frequent level, and points stay raw.

k

Basis dimension for s(): a single integer, or a named list of integers keyed by variable name. -1L (the default) leaves the choice to mgcv. Each cell's basis is capped at the number of distinct predictor values in its rows, and an auto_refit_k refit stops one below that number; capped cells are listed in flags$k_capped and recorded as k_requested, k_used and k_capped.

bs

Basis type for s(); "tp" (thin plate) by default.

engine

"bam" (the default) fits with mgcv::bam(), "gam" with mgcv::gam(). The two differ in their default method and by about one to three percent in EDF on the same data.

method

Smoothing-parameter estimation method passed to mgcv. NULL (the default) resolves to "fREML" for engine = "bam" and "REML" for engine = "gam".

na_action

"pairwise" (the default) fits each cell on the rows complete for its own variables and the adjust columns; "complete" first drops every row with a missing value in any fitted or adjusting column. Infinite values count as missing and are reported in a warning. A pair sharing fewer than 5 complete rows is not fitted and is listed in flags$sparse; an error is raised only when no pair reaches 5 rows.

n_grid

Number of equally spaced points at which each smooth and its derivatives are evaluated, at least 10. NULL (the default) resolves to 200L when derivatives is non-empty and 100L otherwise.

derivatives

Integer vector of derivative orders to compute for every cell, a subset of 1:2. The default 1:2 computes both; integer() computes none.

derivative_ci

The band stored with each derivative curve: "pointwise" (the default), "none" or "simultaneous". Simultaneous bands use the Monte Carlo critical multiplier of Ruppert, Wand and Carroll (2003) as applied to GAMs by Simpson (2018).

derivative_ci_nsim

Number of Monte Carlo draws for derivative_ci = "simultaneous"; 1000L by default and at least 100.

p_adjust

Multiplicity adjustment of the smooth F-test p-values across the k(k - 1) directed cells: "none" (the default), "BH" or "holm", applied once with stats::p.adjust(). Raw and adjusted values are both kept.

shape_cutoffs

Named list of classification thresholds, from janusplot_shape_cutoffs(), mapping the shape indices to a shape_category label.

k_check_thresholds

Named list with entries edf_ratio, k_index and p for the basis-dimension diagnostic that follows mgcv::k.check(). NULL (the default) uses edf_ratio = 0.9, k_index = 1 and p = 0.05.

auto_refit_k

Logical. When TRUE, a cell flagged by the k-check is refitted with a doubled basis until the flag clears, the distinct-value cap is reached or k_max_iter doublings have run. The diagnostic is computed either way; the default is FALSE.

k_max_iter

Maximum number of doublings per cell when auto_refit_k = TRUE; 2L by default.

discrete

Logical. Passes mgcv's covariate discretisation to mgcv::bam(); FALSE by default and ignored for engine = "gam".

nthreads

Integer. Threads used inside each mgcv::bam() fit; 1L by default, which avoids oversubscription under parallel = TRUE. Ignored for engine = "gam".

parallel

Logical. When TRUE, pairs are fitted with future.apply::future_mapply() under the user's future::plan(); FALSE by default.

keep_fits

Logical. When TRUE, the mgcv model objects are kept in $fits and as fit_yx / fit_xy of every pair; FALSE (the default) keeps metrics and prediction grids only.

...

Further arguments passed to mgcv::gam() or mgcv::bam(). The print() and summary() methods ignore them. Under a family with a non-identity link the curve and its band are drawn on the response scale, while the derivatives, the shape indices and the shape label describe the linear predictor (the link scale). The two agree on monotone labels; a curvature label can differ, for example a log-linear Poisson mean is linear_up on the link scale and convex on the response scale. A family applies to every cell of the matrix, so fit count or binary columns in their own call, not beside continuous ones.

x

A janusplot_fit object.

object

A janusplot_fit object.

Value

A list of class janusplot_fit with components, in order:

vars

Character vector of the variables fitted, in matrix order.

pairs

List with one element per unordered pair i < j. Each element carries i, j, var_i, var_j, fit_yx, fit_xy (NULL unless keep_fits = TRUE), the prediction grids pred_yx, pred_xy (data frames with x, fit, se, lo, hi on the response scale, se on the link scale, and fit_link when the link is not the identity), the partial residuals partial_yx, partial_xy (numeric, one per row the cell was fitted on; NULL without adjust or with a non-identity link), edf_yx, edf_xy, association_p_yx, association_p_xy, association_p_adj_yx, association_p_adj_xy, dev_exp_yx, dev_exp_xy, deviance_gap_yx, deviance_gap_xy, n_used, asymmetry_index, k_capped_yx, k_capped_xy, directional_complexity_yx, directional_complexity_xy, the correlations cor_pearson, cor_spearman, cor_kendall and tie_ratio, the shape indices monotonicity_index_*, convexity_index_*, the counts n_turning_*, n_inflect_*, the labels shape_*, shape_code_*, shape_archetype_*, shape_monotonic_*, shape_linear_*, the margins shape_borderline_yx, shape_borderline_xy (NA for an indeterminate or count-decided label), the derivative curves deriv_yx, deriv_xy (lists keyed "1", "2" of data frames with x, fit, se, lo, hi, ci_type), the prediction references prediction_reference_yx, prediction_reference_xy, the k-check lists k_check_yx, k_check_xy, k_requested_*, k_used_*, engine, method, error_yx and error_xy.

table

Data frame with one row per directed cell: var_x, var_y, position ("upper" if var_y is first), n_used, edf, association_p, association_p_adj, signif (glyph from the adjusted p-value), dev_exp, deviance_gap, asymmetry_index, k_capped_yx, k_capped_xy, directional_complexity (signed for this cell), the correlations, the shape indices, counts and labels, shape_borderline, the k-check columns k_prime, k_index, k_p, k_flag, k_check_status, k_initial, k_final, k_iterations, k_at_cap, k_requested, k_used, k_capped, engine, method and error. summary() returns this table.

data

The cleaned copy of the columns used, as described in Details.

adjust

The adjust formula, or NULL.

settings

Named list of the fit settings as resolved: engine, method, k, bs, na_action, n_grid, derivatives, derivative_ci, derivative_ci_nsim, p_adjust, shape_cutoffs, k_check_thresholds, auto_refit_k, k_max_iter, family and link (names, as in stats::family()), discrete and nthreads.

flags

List with failed (data frame of var_x, var_y, reason for cells that carry no fit), k_capped and k_flagged (character vectors of cells as "var_y ~ s(var_x)") and sparse (data frame of var_i, var_j, n_shared for pairs with fewer than 5 shared rows).

fits

When keep_fits = TRUE, the list of mgcv objects keyed "i_j" for the cell vars[j] ~ s(vars[i]); otherwise NULL.

call

The matched call.

print() returns x invisibly; summary() returns the table component.

Details

Suffixes name the direction of fit. _xy is vars[i] ~ s(vars[j]) for i < j, the upper-triangle cell at row i, column j; _yx is vars[j] ~ s(vars[i]), the lower-triangle cell. In $table each row is one directed cell with var_x the predictor and var_y the response.

First and second derivatives of every smooth are computed at fit time by default, so n_grid = NULL resolves to 200 evaluation points. The shape indices M and C, the turning-point and inflection counts and the flat-range ratio are computed on this grid.

The smooth F-test p-values of the directed cells form one family. p_adjust adjusts them once with stats::p.adjust() and the result is stored beside the raw values as association_p_adj. A failed cell has no p-value and stays out of the family, so the family is the cells that produced a p-value, at most k(k - 1). Under "none" the adjusted columns equal the raw ones.

directional_complexity_yx is (EDF_yx - EDF_xy) / (EDF_yx + EDF_xy) in [-1, 1], positive when the fit of var_j on var_i is the more complex direction; directional_complexity_xy is its negative and asymmetry_index its magnitude. A is unreliable when either direction had its basis dimension capped (k_capped_yx or k_capped_xy), either at the first fit or when an auto_refit_k refit reached the cap (k_at_cap in the k-check columns).

shape_borderline is the smallest absolute gap between a shape index and a classification cutoff whose crossing by that index alone would change the shape_category label, on the index's own scale: M and C against the monotonicity and curvature cutoffs, the flat-range ratio against the flat cutoff. A small value marks a label that a slightly different smooth would have moved. Only flat and the monotone labels of a curve with no turning point and no inflection carry a margin. Every other label is decided by the turning-point and inflection counts and has NA: the margin does not measure how near a count is to changing.

$data is the cleaned copy of the columns used: the fitted variables, the adjust variables and every factor, character or logical column of data, under the original column names, after infinite values are set to NA and character or logical adjust columns are converted to factor. It keeps every row under na_action = "pairwise" and the listwise-complete rows under "complete"; a cell's raw points are its two columns on the rows complete for them and the adjust columns.

See also

janusplot() for the matrix, janusplot_shape_metrics() for the shape indices, janusplot_shape_cutoffs() for the classification thresholds.

Other smooth-associations: janusplot(), janusplot_compare(), janusplot_curves(), janusplot_direction(), janusplot_pair(), janusplot_reference(), janusplot_style(), plot.janusplot_compare(), plot.janusplot_fit()

Examples

fit <- janusplot_fit(mtcars[, c("mpg", "hp", "wt")], engine = "gam")
fit
#> janusplot fit: 3 variables (mpg, hp, wt)
#> 3 pairs, 6 directed cells
#> engine = gam, method = REML, adjust = none
#> no flags
#> Largest asymmetries:
#>   hp <-> wt  A = 0.45  wt ~ hp: EDF 3.1, p < 0.001, inverted_u | hp ~ wt: EDF 1.2, p < 0.001, concave_up
#>   mpg <-> wt  A = 0.02  wt ~ mpg: EDF 2.3, p < 0.001, convex_down | mpg ~ wt: EDF 2.4, p < 0.001, convex_down
#>   mpg <-> hp  A = 0.01  hp ~ mpg: EDF 3.0, p < 0.001, s_shape | mpg ~ hp: EDF 3.0, p < 0.001, convex_down
#> Use summary() for the per-cell table and plot() for the matrix.
summary(fit)[, c("var_x", "var_y", "edf", "association_p",
                 "shape_category")]
#>   var_x var_y      edf association_p shape_category
#> 1    hp   mpg 3.011654  0.000000e+00    convex_down
#> 2    wt   mpg 2.400250  0.000000e+00    convex_down
#> 3   mpg    hp 3.048184  1.304169e-06        s_shape
#> 4    wt    hp 1.179943  1.087684e-04     concave_up
#> 5   mpg    wt 2.324136  0.000000e+00    convex_down
#> 6    hp    wt 3.086728  1.966037e-05     inverted_u
fit$pairs[[1L]]$asymmetry_index
#> [1] 0.006028176
